assumptions: the prior raw-C fiber endpoint classification and deficiency indices remain pinned by the upstream result
the real reference initial-value solutions and the limit-circle Wronskian boundary maps exist on the maximal fiber domains under the stated singular Sturm-Liouville hypotheses
joint continuity of finite-Q initial-value solutions in p^2 is used only to establish a measurable reference field, not to identify literal endpoint values
the measurable-resolvent/direct-integral theorem guard requires the stated weak measurability of one nonreal fiber resolvent; its hypotheses and scope must remain explicit
the singleton p=0 is Lebesgue-null and this calculation neither adds an origin atom nor glues p-positive and p-negative sectors
the selected constant reference-boundary line is additional quantization data and is not a unique or physical choice

declared_candidate.direct_integral_domain: D(C_Gamma)={psi: psi(p) in D(C_p,Gamma) a.e. and integral ||C_p,Gamma psi(p)||^2 dp < infinity}
declared_candidate.inherited_raw_C_space: H_C=L2(R_Q times R_phi, f(Q) dQ dphi), f(Q)=12*pi^2*exp(3Q/2)
declared_candidate.selection_status: declared constant line in the real reference coordinates; not derived from H=fC, parity, RAQ, BFV, or a physical principle

exact_calculation.direct_integral: C_Gamma=integral^oplus_R C_p,Gamma dp with graph-norm domain
exact_calculation.p_zero_role: Lebesgue-null; no atom, finite part, quotient, or gluing is constructed

exact_checks.statement: the reference equation has no first derivative, so W(c_p,s_p) is Q-independent
the reference ODE coefficient depends on p only through p^2
with Gamma_0=W(u,s), Gamma_1=-W(u,c), the minus-end form is Gamma_0(u)^*Gamma_1(v)-Gamma_1(u)^*Gamma_0(v)
the declared Gamma_1=0 reference boundary line annihilates the scalar boundary form
ODE uniqueness with even coefficient and identical Q0 data gives c_-p=c_p and s_-p=s_p, hence P preserves Gamma_1=0

numerical_calculation.scope: finite-interval IVP diagnostics for the normalized zero-energy reference pair; not a computation of endpoint boundary limits, a nonreal resolvent, or a raw-C spectral density

numerical_checks.statement: the finite-interval normalized reference IVP preserves W(c_p,s_p)=1 at all bounded p,Q samples
the numerical IVP reference pairs for p and -p agree at all bounded samples

theorem_guards.conclusion_and_scope: the selected boundary graph supplies a measurable self-adjoint fiber field, hence a decomposable extension up to Lebesgue-a.e. equality; this does not classify p-mixing extensions or turn the theorem route into a physical selection principle

theorem_guards.theorem: measurable symmetry-preserving self-adjoint extension and decomposable unbounded-operator criterion
